1.10 How it works

1.10.1 Components

Component Location Responsibility
Core crates/core Read-only source access, the view, the exFAT builder, HTTP, WebDAV, NFS and harvesting; nothing application-specific
PMP plugin plugins/pmp Camera layout, card profiles, timestamp conventions and history filtering
Previews plugin plugins/previews The preview map, DNG and JPEG composition, and ratings capture
Application src/main.rs Config loading, overrides, plugin selection, and the harvest and unmount commands
Launcher bin/diskproxy The background process, mounting, harvesting and the start/status/stop lifecycle

1.10.2 Sources and views

A Source opens its root directory once. Every lookup walks from that descriptor one component at a time with openat and O_NOFOLLOW, rejecting empty components, ., .., embedded slashes and NUL, and returning only read-only regular files and directories. A View combines a source, a plugin and a volume label, and every transport serves through it.

1.10.3 Building the disk

The scan runs in two phases. A serial walk lists every folder and adds a placeholder for each file. Then a parallel phase opens and lays out the files, one directory per task, each file opened relative to its already-open folder, and calls the plugin’s compose for each. A reporter thread prints progress every two seconds on long scans.

The layout keeps each name once, with a link to its parent folder, and rebuilds full paths only when a file is read; each file’s pieces become extents in the disk’s map. After building, the server returns freed startup memory to macOS, so its resident size reflects what it keeps.

A disk read finds the extents covering the requested range: generated metadata, zeros, or ranges of source files. Before reading a source file, it checks that file’s size and modification time against what was recorded at scan time.

1.10.4 The NFS server

The NFS transport is built on the nfsserve crate and runs on tokio. It presents the same view by path. Its overlay keeps client-written files, client-created folders and the paths the client removed or renamed away. Presented metadata is computed on first use. A settle timer passes each written file to the plugin once it has had no writes for two seconds, and a SIGTERM handler flushes the rest.

1.10.5 The launcher

bin/diskproxy starts diskproxy-server serve in the background with its output in the session folder, polls the startup JSON for the disk URL or NFS port, shows scan progress, and mounts. For a writable disk it also starts the harvester and records its arguments, start time and the mount time, so stop can finish or replace it. stop reverses each step and checks identities on the way, so it never detaches a different disk or stops a different process.
